evidence.trl_pathway: Most TRL progressions are reasonable (e.g., S02 TRL4→completion in ~2.75 years, S04 TRL5 in ~2.25 years), but S06 (AI-driven Material Discovery, TRL3) targeting completion by 2030-Q4 in ~2.25 years is aggressive for an architecture-class technology, and dependency violations mean Solid State Electrolytes effectively starts before its prerequisites are met, undermining pathway integrity.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: The portfolio includes genuinely exploratory technologies (TRL3 AI-driven Material Discovery, TRL4 Solid State Electrolytes) alongside enabling process and equipment technologies, which is consistent with a 기술선도 orientation; however, the uniform Tier=High investment across all 7 technologies with identical scores lacks the differentiation expected in a true technology leadership strategy that would concentrate resources on frontier bets.
evidence.competitive_awareness: All selected technologies are squarely within the Cathode Materials / Functional Materials / battery domain, showing strong domain fit; the inclusion of AI-driven material discovery and solid-state electrolytes signals awareness of next-generation competitive frontiers, though there is no explicit evidence of competitor positioning or differentiation rationale beyond technology selection.
evidence.market_timing: For 기술선도, completions 1-2 years before boom are ideal; High-Throughput Battery Testing completes 3.5 years after its boom (2027-Q2), Advanced Battery Packaging is 1.5 years late, Silicon Anode Materials 1.25 years late, and High Nickel Cathode Materials 1.0 year late — only Solid State Electrolytes and Dry Electrode Coating are on-target, representing systematic late-completion issues across the majority of the portfolio.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: The selection of high-nickel cathodes, solid-state electrolytes, and AI-driven discovery reflects technologies with both active patent filing trends and growing market demand, suggesting some convergence awareness; however, the identical market_opp and strategic_fit scores (4.0 and 5.0) for all technologies imply formulaic rather than deliberate convergence-zone targeting, and High-Throughput Battery Testing is more of an enablement tool than a patent-market convergence play.

strengths: Strong domain coherence — all technologies are tightly aligned with the Cathode Materials / Functional Materials core domain, enabling competitive advantage from existing expertise
Inclusion of TRL3-4 frontier technologies (AI-driven Material Discovery, Solid State Electrolytes) demonstrates genuine commitment to long-horizon technology leadership consistent with 기술선도 strategy
weaknesses: Systematic late-completion timing across 5 of 7 technologies (mean error 1.14 years), with High-Throughput Battery Testing completing 3.5 years after its market boom, severely undermining market capture potential
Two hard dependency violations for Solid State Electrolytes (starts 2026-Q2 but requires S01 and S03 completing in 2028-2029) make the roadmap structurally infeasible as planned
missing_technologies: Lithium Metal Anode (complementary to solid-state electrolytes for full solid-state battery stack)
Battery Management System (BMS) AI integration (bridges AI-driven discovery with product-level deployment)
investment_issues: All 7 technologies receive identical scores (market_opp=4.0, strategic_fit=5.0, executability=4.0, uncertainty=3.0, urgency=4.0) and uniform Tier=High allocation, suggesting a lack of genuine portfolio prioritization rather than a strategically differentiated investment thesis

High-Throughput Battery Testing receives the same High-tier investment as frontier R&D technologies despite being an equipment/enablement play with a boom window already past by the time it completes, representing poor capital allocation
timing_issues: High-Throughput Battery Testing (S07) completes at 2030-Q4 but market boom is 2027-Q2 — a 3.5-year delay renders this technology commercially irrelevant at completion
Advanced Battery Packaging completes 1.5 years after its 2028-Q2 boom, and its dependency on both S01 and S02 (which itself has unresolved dependency violations) compounds the delay risk
Solid State Electrolytes is scheduled to start (2026-Q2) before its prerequisites High Nickel Cathode Materials (ends 2028-Q4) and Advanced Battery Packaging (ends 2029-Q4) are completed
